## Contents of this Practice Direction

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Contents of this Practice Direction] Section I –Introduction

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Contents of this Practice Direction] Section II – Routes of appeal

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Contents of this Practice Direction] Section III – General provisions about statutory appeals

## SECTION I – INTRODUCTION

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > SECTION I – INTRODUCTION] 1.1 This Practice Direction applies to all statutory appeals, and to other appeals which are subject to special provision, but not to appeals by way of case stated (to which Practice Direction 52E applies). ## SECTION II – ROUTES OF APPEAL

## 2.1 In this Practice Direction, the court to which an appeal lies is prescribed by statute. ## SECTION III – GENERAL PROVISIONS ABOUT STATUTORY APPEALS

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > SECTION III – GENERAL PROVISIONS ABOUT STATUTORY APPEALS] 3.1 This Section contains general provisions about statutory appeals (paragraphs 3.2 – 3.8). For where this Practice Direction or a statute makes additional special provision see also Section 4. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > SECTION III – GENERAL PROVISIONS ABOUT STATUTORY APPEALS] 3.2 Where any of the provisions in this Section provide for documents to be filed at the appeal court, those documents are in addition to any documents required under Part 52 or Practice Direction 52B or 52C. ## 3.3

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 3.3] Subject to rule 52.9—

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 3.3] Where the appellant wishes to appeal against a decision of the Upper Tribunal, the appellant’s notice must be filed within 28 days of the date on which notice of the Upper Tribunal’s decision on permission to appeal to the Court of Appeal is sent to the appellant. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 3.3] 3.3A Where a statement of reasons for a decision is given later than the notice of that decision, the period for filing the appellant’s notice is calculated from the date on which the statement is sent to the appellant. ## Service of appellant’s notice: rule 52.12(3)

## 3.4

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 3.4] (1) The appellant must serve the appellant’s notice on the respondent and on the chairman of the tribunal, Minister of State, government department or other person from whose decision the appeal is brought. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 3.4] (2) In the case of an appeal from the decision of a tribunal that has no chairman or member who acts as a chairman, the appellant’s notice must be served on the member (or members if more than one) of the tribunal. ## Variation of time: rule 52.15

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Variation of time: rule 52.15] 3.5 Where any statute prescribes a period within which an appeal must be filed then, unless the statute otherwise provides, the appeal court may not extend that period. ## Applications by third parties (rule 52.25)

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Applications by third parties (rule 52.25)] 3.6 Where all the parties consent, the court may deal with an application under rule 52.12A without a hearing. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Applications by third parties (rule 52.25)] 3.7 An application for permission must be made by letter to the relevant court office, identifying the appeal, explaining who the applicant is and indicating why and in what form the applicant wants to participate in the hearing. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Applications by third parties (rule 52.25)] 3.8 If the applicant is seeking a prospective order as to costs, the letter must say what kind of order and on what grounds. ## SECTION IV – SPECIFIC APPEALS

## Provisions about specific appeals

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Provisions about specific appeals] 4.1 This Section sets out special provisions about the appeals listed in the Table below. This Section is not exhaustive and does not create, amend or remove any right of appeal. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Provisions about specific appeals] 4.2 Part 52 applies to all appeals to which this Section applies subject to any special provisions set out in this Section. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > Provisions about specific appeals] 4.3 Where any of the provisions in this Section provide for documents to be filed at the appeal court, these documents are in addition to any documents required under Part 52 or Practice Direction 52B or 52C. ## Certain appeals to the High Court to be heard in Chancery Division

## APPEALS TO THE COURT OF APPEAL

## 6.1

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 6.1] (1) The appellant must file the appellant’s notice at the Court of Appeal within 28 days after the date on which the decree was pronounced or conditional order made. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 6.1] (2) The appellant must file the following documents with the appellant’s notice –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 6.1] (a) the decree or conditional order; and

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 6.1] (b) a certificate of service of the appellant’s notice. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 6.1] (3) The appellant’s notice must be served on the appropriate District Judge (see sub-paragraph (6)) in addition to the persons to be served under rule 52.12(3) and in accordance with that rule. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 6.1] (4) The lower court may not alter the time limits for filing of the appeal notices. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 6.1] (5) Where an appellant intends to apply to the Court of Appeal for an extension of time for serving or filing the appellant’s notice the appellant must give notice of that intention to the appropriate District Judge (see sub-paragraph 6) before the application is made. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 6.1] (6) In this paragraph ‘the appropriate District Judge’ means, where the lower court is –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 6.1] (a) the County Court, the District Judge of the County Court hearing centre in question;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 6.1] (b) a district registry, the District Judge of that registry;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 6.1] (c) the Principal Registry of the Family Division, the senior District Judge of that division. ## 7.1

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (1) This paragraph applies to any appeal to the Court of Appeal relating to the application Chapter I or Chapter II of Part I of the Competition Act 1998. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (2) In this paragraph –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (a) ‘the 1988 Act’ means the Competition Act 1998 or to a claim under section 101 of the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (aa) ‘the 2024 Act’ means the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (b) Omitted

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (c) Omitted

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (d) “competition “authority” means —

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (i) the Competition and Markets Authority; or

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (ii) a regulator as defined in section 54 of the 1988 Act;

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (e) Omitted

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (3) Any party whose appeal notice raises an issue relating to the application of Chapter I or II of Part I of the 1998 Act or to a claim under section 101 of the 2024 Act, must –

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (a) state that fact in the appeal notice; and

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (b) serve a copy of the appeal notice on the Competition and Markets Authority (addressed to the General Counsel, the Competition and Markets Authority, The Cabot, 25 Cabot Square, London, E14 4QZ. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (4) Omitted

[Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (5) A  competition authority may make written observations to the Court of Appeal, or apply for permission to make oral observations, on issues relating to the application of Chapter I or II of the 1998 Act. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (5A) The Competition and Markets Authority may make written observations to the Court of Appeal, or apply for permission to make oral observations, on issues relating to a claim under section 101 of the 2024 Act. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (6) If a competition authority intends to make written observations to the Court of Appeal, it must give notice of its intention to do so by letter to the Civil Appeals Office at the earliest opportunity. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (7) An application by a competition authority for permission to make oral representations at the hearing of an appeal must be made by letter to the Civil Appeals Office at the earliest opportunity, identifying the appeal and indicating why the applicant wishes to make oral representations. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (8) If a competition authority files a notice under sub-paragraph (6) or an application under sub-paragraph (7), it must at the same time serve a copy of the notice or application on every party to the appeal. [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (9) Any request by a competition authority for the court to send it any documents relating to an appeal should be made at the same time as filing a notice under sub-paragraph (6) or an application under sub-paragraph (7). [Practice Direction 52D – statutory appeals and appeals subject to special provision > 7.1] (10) When the Court of Appeal receives a notice under sub-paragraph (6) it may give case management directions to the competition authority, including directions about the date by which any written observations are to be filed.
